lead: System testing checks the complete product against its requirements. Acceptance testing checks whether the customer will actually use it. Debugging finds and repairs the cause after a failure. These steps exist because unit and integration tests check parts, not the whole journey or user fit. A team uses them before releasing a UPI app, an IRCTC booking flow or banking software. System testing catches end-to-end gaps; acceptance testing gives the customer a measurable gate; debugging turns a reported failure into a repaired fault.
prereq: You need: Chapter 4.5 on unit and integration testing, and Unit 2 on requirements.

blocks.text: System testing checks the complete, integrated product against the requirements. Unit and integration tests check parts; system testing checks the whole journey. A test case has preconditions, steps and one expected outcome, which you may check with several assertions. Scenario testing designs system tests from end-to-end user stories. For a UPI app: log in, add a beneficiary, transfer ₹500 from account A (balance ₹2,000) to account B (balance ₹1,000), and check both balances. The single outcome is that the transfer completes and money is conserved: A = ₹1,500, B = ₹1,500 and total money = ₹3,000.

System testing also checks system qualities. Recovery: cut power during a transfer and restart; the app must not debit twice. Security: a user without login must not see another user's balance. Performance, stress, configuration and usability tests are in Chapter 4.8. Documentation testing checks the user guide, help text and error messages against the real screen. If help says 'tap Send Money' but the button says 'Pay', the document has a defect. System testing is verification at product level: the product must satisfy the requirements written in the SRS. Whether the product meets the user's real need is judged later, by acceptance testing. See Chapter 4.2.

sections.h3: Acceptance testing with users and contracts

blocks.text: Acceptance testing asks whether the customer will use the product. The customer, not the developer, judges it. User acceptance testing (UAT) uses real users on realistic tasks. In the example, 20 users each make 3 transfers; at least 18 of 20 must complete all 3 without help. That is 18 ÷ 20 = 90% of users.

items: Alpha testing happens at the developer's site. Intended users try the product while developers watch and record problems.
Beta testing happens at the user's site with real data and less control. Some syllabi call these alpha-beta tests.
Contract acceptance runs tests written in the contract.
Regulation acceptance checks rules from a regulator, such as a central bank's rules for a payment app.

blocks.text: Acceptance criteria must be measurable. 'Works well' is not a criterion. '18 of 20 users finish 3 transfers without help' is a criterion. UAT verifies fitness for use; it is not a hunt for coding faults. Alpha and beta are acceptance tests, not system tests.

Debugging is not testing. Testing finds a failure: actual behaviour differs from expected behaviour. Debugging finds the fault that caused the failure and repairs it. A fault is the defect in the code; a failure is what the user sees. The loop is: reproduce the failure, diagnose the cause, repair the code, then run regression tests. Regression testing is in Chapter 4.7.

items: Brute force: add print statements or logging, read memory dumps, and narrow the place where values go wrong.
Backtracking: start at the failure and walk backwards through the code until the first wrong value appears.
Cause elimination: list possible causes, design a test for each, and remove causes one by one.

blocks.text: A defect bash is a short, focused session where the whole team hunts for as many defects as possible in the running product. It is a group testing activity that feeds the debugging loop; it is not a separate test level. Program analysis tools inspect code statically or at run time. Symbolic execution runs code with symbols instead of numbers. Model checking explores system states against a property. Only a few universities teach the proofs; know the idea: automated help to locate faults.

figure.caption: The ₹500 UPI transfer from A (₹2,000) to B (₹1,000) passes system testing with A = ₹1,500 and B = ₹1,500 (total ₹3,000); acceptance needs 18 of 20 users to pass (90%). A failed acceptance report enters the debugging loop: reproduce, diagnose, repair, regression test, then rerun system testing.

spec.title: System test, acceptance and debugging loop
spec.aria: A vertical flow from requirements to system test and acceptance test; a failed acceptance report goes to reproduce, diagnose cause, repair, regression test, then back to system test.

examples.question: A UPI app must transfer money between two accounts. System test: transfer ₹500 from account A (balance ₹2,000) to B (balance ₹1,000); expected A = ₹1,500 and B = ₹1,500. Acceptance test: 20 users each make 3 transfers; at least 18 of 20 must complete all 3 without help. During acceptance, one transfer shows B = ₹1,000 after the app says success. Write the debugging steps and the regression test to run after the fix.
steps: Acceptance: 20 users × 3 transfers = 60 attempts. Pass if at least 18 users complete all 3: 18 ÷ 20 × 100 = 90%.
Failure: app says success but B stays ₹1,000. Reproduce with the same starting balances and the same ₹500 transfer; record A and B after each step.
Diagnose: trace the transfer path; find where the debit commits but the credit does not. A likely cause is that the credit update fails or is not committed, and the error is ignored.
Repair: put debit and credit in one transaction; commit only when both succeed; on error roll back and show a failure message.
Regression: rerun the original ₹500 transfer, the failed-credit case, a double-transfer test, and the chosen old tests from Chapter 4.7.
examples.answer: Expected balances are A = ₹1,500 and B = ₹1,500 (total ₹3,000); the acceptance threshold is 18 of 20 users = 90%, and the failure needs a transaction fix plus regression tests.

traps: Calling debugging 'testing again'. Testing finds a failure; debugging finds the fault and repairs it.
Fixing only the success message when the balance update is wrong. That hides the symptom and leaves the fault.
Calling beta testing a system test. Beta testing is acceptance testing at the user's site.
Using UAT as a hunt for coding faults. Unit, integration and system tests find code faults; UAT judges fitness for use.
Treating a defect bash as a test level. A defect bash is a focused group search for failures; diagnosis and repair come afterwards, followed by regression tests.

quiz.q: Define system testing in one sentence.
quiz.a: System testing checks the complete, integrated product against its requirements, end to end.

quiz.q: State two differences between alpha and beta testing.
quiz.a: Alpha runs at the developer's site with developers watching; beta runs at the user's site with real data and less control. Both are acceptance tests.

quiz.q: Account A has ₹2,000 and B has ₹1,000. A ₹250 transfer goes from A to B. Give the expected balances and total.
An app says success but B is unchanged. Why is changing the success message not debugging?
quiz.a: The failure is the wrong balance, not the message. Debugging must reproduce the transfer, find why credit is not committed or updated, and repair that fault; otherwise money is still wrong.

quiz.q: 20 users each make 3 transfers. 17 users complete all 3 without help. The pass mark is 18 users. Pass or fail, and what percentage passed?
A team holds a defect bash and records 30 failures in one day. Is this a test level? Explain.
quiz.a: No. A defect bash is a focused group search for failures, not a test level. The faults are diagnosed and repaired afterwards, followed by regression tests.

beyond: Not for the exam. Industry links bug reports to reproduction steps, logs and distributed traces so debugging starts from evidence. Static analysers and sanitizers catch faults before release, and model checkers are used on payment and embedded code where states must obey strict properties.
